clinician.final_diagnosis: superior Foville syndrome due to a pontine hemorrhage
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old patient presented with abrupt onset of left body side weakness, acute headaches, and rotatory vertigo. Neurological examination revealed right oculomotor paralysis, right facial palsy, and left hemiparesis sparing the face, consistent with superior Foville syndrome. A brain CT scan confirmed a spontaneous hemorrhage in the right pontine's posterolateral part, compressing the fourth ventricle. The patient received symptomatic treatment including antalgic, anxiolytic, laxative, and physiotherapy, leading to clinical improvement. The patient was discharged 10 days later. The underlying etiology of the pontine hemorrhage (e.g., vascular malformation, coagulopathy, or cryptogenic origin) was not documented despite attempts to investigate.
